food.name: Plums
sourceNotes: USDA FoodData Central 169949, Plums, raw, per 100g.
Daily value percentages are derived from USDA nutrients using FDA adult DVs and rounded to the nearest whole percent.
Glycemic index is a context value derived from International GI Database raw/unspecified plum entries rather than USDA nutrient data.

topPros.title: easy fresh-fruit snack
topPros.explanation: It works with no peeling or cooking, so it is easy to use when the fruit is ripe.

topPros.title: peel adds tart colour
topPros.explanation: Keeping the skin gives more plum colour, texture, and sharp-sweet contrast.

topPros.title: works fresh or cooked
topPros.explanation: It can go into yoghurt, oats, salads, compote, sauces, or desserts without much effort.

topCons.title: bruises easily
topCons.explanation: Soft fruit bruises quickly, so quality can drop fast after transport or storage.

topCons.title: ripeness window is short
topCons.explanation: The best eating window is narrow, and underripe or overripe plums are much less useful.

topCons.title: stone interrupts snacking
topCons.explanation: The pit makes them less convenient than fully edible bite-size fruit like berries or grapes.

explanation.summary: Fats are carrying this food most, while minerals are holding it back most. It lands in D tier.
explanation.whyThisTier: This food lands in D tier with a display score of 20. Section scores: fats 50, carbs 46.7, proteins 20, vitamins 8, minerals 0, pros 50, cons 50.
